title: Trace-driven playbook authoring and PagerDuty/Slack feedback loop
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: When incidents fire, SREs and on-call engineers spend too much time manually gathering traces, correlating slow spans with error bursts, and writing the initial postmortem. There is no structured feedback channel from postmortems back into alert thresholds or playbooks. This causes repeated noise and slower incident resolution.

Goal: Build an integrated flow that (a) harvests traced evidence and top suspect spans at incident time, (b) auto-generates a draft playbook / postmortem seed with recommended mitigations and alert-tuning suggestions, and (c) surfaces those suggestions via PagerDuty and Slack with one-click actions to apply or schedule alert updates. The flow should preserve privacy and be auditable.

Scope: tracing hooks, metrics/log correlation pipeline, runtime dashboard integration, PagerDuty enrichment fields and Slack interactive messages, draft postmortem generation, and a safe "apply suggestion" pathway for alert configs. Exclude: full automated alert edits without human approval and external customer-facing incident communications.
technical_spec:
High-level data flow: 1) Incident detected by existing alerting pipeline (metrics or error rate). 2) Orchestration service calls Trace Hook API to request a targeted snapshot: highest-latency traces in N minutes window + error-tagged traces. 3) Trace enrichment service runs a lightweight analysis: fingerprint traces, rank top 5 suspect spans by combined score (latency contribution, error co-occurrence, frequency). 4) Correlate with logs and metrics using correlation keys (trace_id, request_id, service/route). 5) Draft playbook generator composes: summary, top suspects with sample span snippets, suggested rollback/mitigation steps, suggested alert threshold changes (metric, aggregator, window), and links to relevant runs/PRs. 6) Postmortem seed is stored in the Postmortem Store and attached to the PagerDuty incident as an enrichment field and pushed to the incident's Slack channel as an interactive card.

Ranking algorithm sketch: combined_score = w1 * p99_delta_rank + w2 * error_cooccurrence_rank + w3 * span_frequency_rank. We will start with w1=0.5, w2=0.35, w3=0.15 and tune via labeled incidents.

Trace sampling: to limit cost, request targeted sampling for N=300 traces in a 5 minute window for the affected service(s) and use adaptive sampling if traffic low. Respect customer VPC/private filters: do not export raw traces outside private network; instead export redacted summaries.

APIs and hooks: - /trace-hooks/snapshot POST (service, window, filters) - /playbooks/draft POST (incident_id, trace_summary, suggested_actions) - PagerDuty enrichment integration via Events API + custom_incident_fields - Slack: interactive message with buttons [View Draft, Apply Alert Suggestion, Schedule Follow-up, Attach to Postmortem].

Console UI: new "Incident Suggestions" drawer on the incident timeline showing suspect spans, delta charts (latency/error), and a one-click "Open Draft" and "Apply Suggestion" that triggers a review modal. Audit log entry required for any action that applies changes.

Operational considerations: run the ranking service in the Observability namespace with autoscaling, limit CPU to 0.5 core per replica initially, and cap memory at 512MB. Add feature flag to gate production rollout. Store drafts with 30d retention and provide export to Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: When an alert of type latency/error fires, the orchestration service successfully triggers a trace snapshot request and stores a trace summary within 30s of alert creation
Playbook generator creates a draft with at least 3 suggested mitigation steps and 1 alert-tuning recommendation for >=90% of incidents in the staging test set
PagerDuty incidents created during tests include the postmortem seed in a custom incident field and show a link to view the full draft
Slack interactive card renders in the incident channel and the Apply Alert Suggestion button opens a review modal (no automatic edits in first rollout)
Audit logs capture who viewed and who accepted a suggestion; attempts to apply suggestions create an audit entry and a GitHub PR for alert rule changes in the alerts repo
Automated redaction ensures no PII/raw payloads are exported for Private deployments; compliance tests pass
End-to-end integration tested in staging with simulated incident generator and performance under 50 concurrent incidents without increased P99 latency on the ranking service (>500ms would fail)
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged alpha in staging for internal SRE team (2 weeks): enable full generation but disable apply button. 2) Closed beta with selected teams and PagerDuty integration (3 weeks): enable interactive Slack cards and manual PR generation for alert updates. 3) Wider beta with on-call rotation (2 weeks): enable 'Apply Suggestion' to create draft PR and a single-owner merge workflow. 4) GA (after 2 successful betas + security review): enable full audit trail and default 30d draft retention. Each phase gated by metrics: false positive rate of suggestions <10% and <5% latency added to orchestration path.
migration_steps: Register trace-hook endpoints and update orchestration service to call snapshot API behind feature flag
Provision ranking service namespace and deploy draft generator with minimal resources
Create PagerDuty custom fields schema and Slack workflow app with OAuth scopes
Seed initial tuning weights and run 100 synthetic incidents to create baseline labels
Enable draft storage and Confluence export integration for postmortem seeds
